name: Eric Flores
contest: Texas CD-34 Republican Primary, March 3, 2026 (general election November 3, 2026)

biography.currentRole: Attorney, private practice (joined O'Hanlon, Demerath & Castillo law firm after leaving DOJ)
priorRoles: Assistant U.S. Attorney, Southern District of Texas, McAllen Criminal Division (career prosecutor, not political appointee — served approximately 2021 to early 2025 across both Trump and Biden administrations)
Texas Army National Guard, Infantry Captain; commanded soldiers during Operation Guardian Support along U.S.-Mexico border
Attorney representing La Joya Independent School District and other municipal clients
biography.education: B.A., University of Texas at Austin; J.D., Texas Southern University Thurgood Marshall School of Law
biography.family: Father Ismael 'Kino' Flores was a Democratic Texas state legislator (convicted on financial disclosure felonies in 2010). Paternal grandfather was first mayor of Sullivan City; maternal grandfather was mayor of Palmview for nearly 20 years. Married with two children. Christian faith.
biography.background: Rio Grande Valley native; Spanish-speaking; prosecuted cartel-connected operations, human smuggling, and white-collar crime as AUSA; border security experience via National Guard deployment. Recently switched party registration from Democrat to Republican. Has described his values as rooted in 'faith, family, and country' and said 'that's not the Democratic Party today.'

statedPositions.quote: championing law enforcement and veteran issues

Listed as third priority. No specific policy mechanisms stated on website. Trump endorsement text he accepted explicitly includes 'cut taxes and regulations, promote made-in-the-USA products, advance American energy dominance.' Listed as fourth of four headline priorities. Implies protecting Social Security and Medicare from cuts but no specific mechanism stated. Notably does not use reform or modernize language. Strategically important given the district's large elderly Hispanic population.

votingRecord.notes: First-time candidate with no legislative voting record. Career was as a federal prosecutor in the executive branch and as a Guard officer — not an elected officeholder. AUSA role is non-partisan by statute.

scorecards.notes: Texas Alliance for Life endorsed Eric D. Flores (R) for U.S. Representative District 34 in the 2026 primary. This organization endorses only candidates who oppose abortion and support pro-life legislation. This is the single highest-signal data point for the reproductive rights axis. Tier 3 (endorsement), but Texas Alliance for Life is a single-issue organization — endorsement is functionally equivalent to a pro-life scorecard grade.

NBPC endorsed Eric Flores; Flores cited this endorsement publicly at the Coastal Candidate Rumble forum. NBPC is known for hardline immigration enforcement positions and endorsed Trump in 2016 and 2020. Signals strong border enforcement position.

No NRA grade found — expected for a first-time candidate with no prior elected office. Cannot score firearms axis from absence, but Trump endorsement and faith/family/country framing are indirect signals.
No LCV score — first-time candidate with no environmental voting record.
As of research date, Eric Flores had not completed the Ballotpedia 2026 Candidate Connection survey. No structured policy responses available through that channel.

endorsements.notes: Trump called Flores an 'America First Patriot' who 'knows the Wisdom and Courage it takes to Ensure LAW AND ORDER.' Trump endorsement text (via trumpstruth.org): 'in Congress, Eric will fight to grow the economy, cut taxes and regulations, promote made-in-the-USA products, advance American energy dominance, keep the border secure, and stop migrant crime.' Flores accepted enthusiastically on X: 'I look forward to working with you to keep our border secure, to stand up for law enforcement, and to put South Texas and America First!' Following the endorsement, at least three rival Republican candidates (Jay Nagy, Fred Hinojosa, Scott Mandel) dropped out and endorsed Flores. NRCC spokesman: 'Flores will help Republicans deliver secure borders, energy dominance, and a strong economy for South Texans.'
Major Texas anti-abortion single-issue organization. Endorsement is a strong signal of pro-life position on reproductive rights axis.
Union representing approximately 16,000 Border Patrol agents. Known for hardline enforcement-first immigration positioning. Flores cited this endorsement prominently at public forums.
TX-34 is one of 26 NRCC target seats for 2026 midterms. NRCC actively promoting Flores as their preferred nominee.
Texas Governor backing adds to institutional Republican support.
House Speaker endorsement. Rep. Tom Emmer also backed Flores on X: 'He will be a strong, reliable voice in our conference and an effective partner in advancing President Trump's agenda. #TX34'
Entrepreneur who had raised over $1 million dropped out following Trump endorsement and backed Flores. Field largely consolidated around Flores post-December 2025.

fundraising.notes: Approximately $1.29M raised; approximately $872K+ reported through December 2025 per FEC filings. Led the field before and after Trump endorsement caused consolidation.

controversies.topic: Party switch and Biden DOJ service
controversies.description: Flores recently switched from Democrat to Republican registration. Served as AUSA through early 2025 spanning both the Biden and Trump DOJ eras. Opponents, particularly Mayra Flores, attacked him as a 'former Democrat, Biden DOJ attorney.' Texas Politics (October 2025) ran a piece suggesting prior social media posts praising Biden and Harris could hurt him. Flores maintains he was a career prosecutor serving across administrations, not a Biden political appointee. On inauguration day claim: Mayra Flores alleged he attended Biden's inauguration; Flores' campaign denied it, stating he was on Guard duty in Victoria that day.
controversies.significanceForScoring: Low direct relevance to civic axis scoring. Does not change his stated policy positions. Signals he may not be a lifelong movement conservative — recent convert. Does not contradict any axis scoring.

controversies.description: Raw Story reported Flores was lead defense counsel for Edinburg Consolidated Independent School District employees in a civil lawsuit accusing them of trauma and abuse of a student (coach alleged to have made a child exercise without clothes). Flores filed a plea to the jurisdiction arguing governmental immunity barred the claims. He subsequently withdrew from the case.
controversies.significanceForScoring: Legal representation controversy, not a personal policy position. Does not affect any civic axis score.

positionConflicts.topic: Immigration — enforcement messaging vs. labor market pragmatism
positionConflicts.conflict: Campaign emphasizes strict border enforcement and stopping migrant crime per Trump endorsement language and NBPC backing. However, multiple interview quotes show Flores explicitly calling for efficient legal immigration pathways to address Rio Grande Valley labor shortages. These are logically reconcilable (enforce the border, streamline legal pathways) but create tension between primary-base messaging and stated nuance. Scorer should note: his immigration position is better characterized as enforcement-plus-legal-pathways rather than pure restrictionism.
sources: Texas Voice forum Feb 2026 (legal immigration personal framing)
Fox News campaign launch (Trump alignment framing)

contextualNotes.districtCharacter: TX-34 is a heavily Hispanic district (90%+) along the Gulf Coast from Corpus Christi to Brownsville. Post-redistricting, it now leans Republican by approximately 10 points in presidential performance (Trump won old lines by 5 in 2024; would have won new lines by approximately 10). District has significant agriculture, maritime manufacturing, and steel industries — hence Flores' labor-immigration nuance.
contextualNotes.primaryDynamics: Flores vs. Mayra Flores primary is a proxy fight between Trump/establishment GOP infrastructure and local RGV Republican base. Eric Flores has national establishment support; Mayra Flores ran twice before and has local RGV Republican name recognition. Eric Flores won the South Padre Island forum straw poll 46-27. Primary is March 3, 2026.
contextualNotes.generalElectionContext: Winner faces incumbent Democrat Vicente Gonzalez in November 2026. District is now GOP-leaning but not safe. A University of Texas poll (Feb 2026) found Democrats leading the generic congressional ballot among Texas Hispanic voters 50-31%, suggesting potential headwinds for any Republican nominee.

evidenceSummary.notes: Flores is a first-time candidate with no legislative voting record. The two highest-signal data points are: (1) Texas Alliance for Life endorsement confirms pro-life position; (2) Trump endorsement text he explicitly accepted names his policy agenda across economic, energy, and border axes. Beyond those anchors, most axis evidence is inferred from endorsement patterns, party alignment, and general rhetorical framing. The main substantive nuance is his explicitly pragmatic (not purely restrictionist) stance on legal immigration — he is on record in multiple venues supporting efficient legal pathways for Valley labor needs. Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Texas Tribune reporting (Feb 26, 2026) confirms there is 'little daylight between candidates on issues' in this primary — all GOP candidates share a standard Trump-era Republican profile. Scorer should score only axes with genuine evidence and omit housing, health cost control, and health public health entirely.
